page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No margin notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: dicit Iehouah exercituum, Non est vltra sapientia in Teman perijt consilium à filijs, corrupta est sapientia eorum? Et eodem capite, versu 22. de terrore tam vulgi quàm optimatum, ait: Ecce tanquam Aquila ascendet hostis, & volabit, & expandet alas suas super Bosrah[?]: eritq; cor fortium Edom in die illa sicut cor mulieris afflictæ.
main_text.head: QVID, AIT PIA MENS, hic discam?
main_text.p: 1. Non metuendam nobis esse astutiam hostium fidei nostrę: tum quia Deus simplices custodit, Psal.116.6. tum quia Deus abolet sapientiam (sic astuciam filiorum seculi æquiuocè vocat) sapientium, & intelligentiam intelligentium è medio tollit. Vbi sapiens? vbi scriba? vbi conquisitor seculi istius? Nonne infatuauit Deus sapientiam seculi istius? Isa.29.14. 1. Cor.1.19.20.

2. Rectè dictum à beato Hieronymo: Prudentia absque simplicitate, malitia est: & simplicitas absq; ratione stultitia. Ideò Deum oremus vt is nobis det, vt reuera simus prudentes vt serpentes, & innocentes vt columbæ, Matth. 10.16.
3. Sit autem nobis antidotum aduersus persuasionem de nostra prudentia, in prō-tu,quod Chrysostomus alicubi hoc Aphorismo indicauit: Prudens nō semper videt,

page.notes: Running head and page number read clearly. The superscript "22" after "versu" is printed small and is copied as a numeral. "Bosrah" is printed with a long s and may be a printer's spelling variant; marked [?]. The hyphenated "prō-tu,quod" is copied as printed, with the printed hyphen and no added spaces. The heading "QVID, AIT PIA MENS," is in spaced capitals with the italic line "hic discam?" beneath it. "Isa.29.14." reads "1sa" in print; the initial is taken as I.
